crashInvestigation.original: Two GPU subprocess crashes with exit -2147483645 (0x80000003) were recorded in PR #112. Windows Application event 1001 at 07:12:40.532Z referenced a separate native llama-server RADAR_PRE_LEAK_64 event. No matching graphics-driver reset event was available.
crashInvestigation.followup: Short original and intermediate portable runs did not reproduce the GPU crash. The intermediate CPU runner working set fell from 2,971,811,840 to 2,932,842,496 bytes across nine samples. Whisper fell from 132,870,144 to 122,712,064 bytes. This interval cannot establish the long-term trend or a GPU crash cause.

original.observation: CPU, Vulkan and Gemini reproduced the static Windows capture failure before the request stage. The decoded frame contained pixels while the next video-frame callback did not arrive in the test interval.

intermediate.provenance: Recorded build source and pre-launch EXE hash. The intermediate EXE recorder lacked an embedded release commit.

checks.observed: Screen result recognized fixture markers. Synthetic transcription persisted. Both native processes stopped.
Gemini Live stayed connected. Screen capture reached HTTP and the selected 3.8 Flash returned 503 on all three attempts.
Screen request reached Mistral and returned HTTP 402.
Vulkan loaded and screen capture reached native inference. The 54-second request timeout was observed.

scenarios.reason: No physical Windows 10 22H2 x64 machine was available.
The candidate launched and the sandboxed smoke reopened synthetic History. The 15-minute physical session and operator History check were unavailable.
Operator availability limited testing to short runs. The intermediate portable reached Gemini HTTP, which returned 503 after three attempts. The required 1h, 4h and 8h active checkpoints are absent.
The laptop was available for short retests only. Text, transcription and vision passed the local request checks. The one-hour hosted rerun on this EXE is pending.

Cached startup, typed inference, transcription, image inference and runner shutdown completed in the Windows CLI harness. A physical disconnect would cut remote access. No one-hour run or active one-hour checkpoint was collected.

The intermediate portable reached the native image route and timed out at 54 seconds. The upgraded runner returned image results in the app CLI code and exited. No one-hour run or active one-hour checkpoint was collected.
A removable audio device was unavailable for the active-device removal and restoration sequence. The new-runner CLI check used synthetic PCM.
Wi-Fi and tethered Ethernet were both active during the physical attempt. Disconnecting both would have cut remote access. Local retry and cancellation tests provide supporting evidence.
The operator reported sleep, wake, lock and unlock. The earlier recorder and Windows event check did not confirm the transition. A verified rerun was unavailable.
The Windows laptop had one integrated display. A second physical display was unavailable for Active Display and pinned-display removal.
Portable smoke supports layout and capture checks under Chromium scale overrides. An operator run at 100%, 125%, 150% and 200% Windows display settings with pixel comparison was unavailable.
A signed-in screen-sharing application and second participant for a private test were unavailable.

Gemini returned 503 and Mistral returned 402 for the intermediate portable. Those statuses establish provider availability and payment failures respectively. No safely observable live 429 or usable Mistral evaluation entitlement was available.

The original portable passed this scenario. The current production downloader passed a command-line interruption and retry against the official Whisper archive in an isolated profile. The rebuilt EXE’s physical cancellation and retry are pending.
